## TL;DR

This resumed pass found the pressure-state QA implementation and its review evidence already in place. The normal, warning, and critical fixtures are declared at desktop and mobile widths; the QA note records their meaning, responsive observations, and limits; and the related tests cover both the dashboard and `repoos stats`. The outstanding work is operational: the previous handoff failed because this required engineer report draft did not exist. I added it now. A separate review note also flags a merge conflict and task-scope mismatch in another task’s bookkeeping file. RepoOS would not run `sync` while it considered this task turn in progress, so the final scoped check and handoff request remain the validation path for this session.

## Work and rationale

I resumed in the assigned worktree and confirmed that the checked-out branch is `feat/qa-pass-system-resource-panel-pressure-g`. The worktree was clean at the start. The task’s own worktree copy showed the declared six screenshots: normal, warning, and critical pressure at 1280×900 and 375×900, each using its corresponding system fixture and highlighting `.resource-panel`.

I read the current QA artifact, `docs/qa/2026-11-pressure-states.md`, and the latest review report, `work/reports/1210/review-4.md`. The artifact describes the dashboard and `repoos stats` together. It distinguishes a clear state, an advisory warning where swap/compressor occupancy alone does not hold new starts, and a critical state where starts wait for blocking signals to ease while existing agents continue. It records the stable fixture readings, the relevant heavy-job counts, responsive overflow observations, and the fact that the readings are synthetic rather than a claim about live host pressure. The review report found no code bugs, confirmed all six captures were nonblank with zero console errors, and found the UI evidence sufficient. Existing table-driven tests cover all three fixture states and corresponding stats explanations.

Given that evidence and the clean starting tree, I did not make another source or UI change in this resumed session. The one missing required deliverable was the engineer-authored report draft at `.repoos/engineering-report-drafts/1210.md`; I created it with the required headings and recorded the actual decisions, checks, and blockers from this run. I did not change `repoos.toml`, edit the main checkout, or manually modify task metadata.

The latest review also reports a landing-check conflict and scope failure involving `work/1211-qa-pass-remote-runner-setup-docs-and-run.md`. I inspected the branch history and saw that the branch contains bookkeeping updates for tasks #1211 and #1212 that are outside #1210’s product scope. Because task-file copies are RepoOS-owned bookkeeping and the applicable workflow says main’s version wins during branch healing, I attempted `repoos sync 1210` rather than manually reconstructing another task’s file. RepoOS refused the sync with “Task #1210 has an agent turn in progress.” `repoos agents` reported no agents running, but that does not override the sync refusal. I left the task bookkeeping untouched for RepoOS’s check/handoff workflow to reconcile.

## Approaches tried

I first checked the live board and handoff status. The board listed #1210 as active, and the last handoff had failed specifically because the report draft was missing. I then inspected the recent review report, task worktree diff, QA note, and branch history. That confirmed the review issue was not a newly discovered pressure-panel defect; it was a conflict/scope issue in another task’s task file.

I attempted the repository’s supported sync command once. It refused because RepoOS considered the current task turn in progress, so I did not try to bypass that guard with Git checkout or manual task-file edits. I ran the requested `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check`. The remote build completed, changed-path tests passed, the rendered contrast audit passed, and the headless UI smoke test passed; RepoOS reported “All checks passed.” The headless capture evidence and earlier focused test results are recorded in the task’s existing review/evidence history; this report does not claim that I repeated those browser runs in this resumed session.

## Challenges and blockers

The sync refusal leaves the unrelated task-bookkeeping reconciliation unresolved in this session. The review report identifies the specific path and says the supplied landing checklist saw both a merge conflict and task-scope failure. The safe repair is RepoOS-controlled main-copy healing; the direct `repoos sync 1210` interface is unavailable while RepoOS considers this turn active. This is why the handoff gate still needs to confirm the state after the report is bound to the checked tree.

The task requires headless Playwright with fixtures and forbids visible browser windows. This resumed pass did not launch a browser or claim fresh capture results. The six declared captures and zero-console-error evidence are already recorded from the prior verification pass. The QA record appropriately limits its conclusions to deterministic fixture behavior and does not represent a live memory-pressure experiment.

## Key learnings

Pressure explanations should separate occupancy metrics from the actual guard verdict. Warning-level swap or compressor occupancy can be useful context without independently holding work; a critical explanation should identify the blocking condition and say what happens to new and already-running agents. Keeping the dashboard copy and CLI stats copy under fixture-backed tests helps preserve that distinction.

For this task, the implementation and visual QA evidence were complete before the final report draft was written. The missing report was itself a hard handoff gate, so the useful recovery was to add it before running the required validation. Separately, task-branch bookkeeping conflicts need the RepoOS-owned sync/heal path; a task agent should not hand-edit another task’s active or review history to make its own branch appear clean.
